beats: 1. Hook warning to camera: don't use ChatGPT; I know you all use it and so did I, but you have to hear this, listen carefully.
2. Reason 1 – accuracy: people use ChatGPT because it supposedly has 'all' the information, but nobody asks how accurate that information really is.

3. Reason 2 – it doesn't really help you learn: personal university example of photographing study material and sending it so ChatGPT says what to circle on a test when cheating, how to learn something faster, or makes a study plan. That's a big mistake.

4. Product pivot: 'There's a much better solution for you: the Memo AI app. I'll put a picture of it somewhere here.' Logo/screenshot overlay appears. CTA: everyone go to memoai.eu right now. Enthusiastic pitch: you just photograph your study material and it makes a summary (notes), quizzes and flashcards with questions, so you learn in literally 2 days what used to take you 2–3 weeks.

5. Reason 3 – over-reliance on AI: research at Stanford and universities around the world found that kids and people today learn much worse, are interested in far fewer things, and develop critical thinking, logic and creativity more slowly because they rely too much on ChatGPT.

6. Reason 4 – privacy, 'maybe the most important one': nobody knows how ChatGPT stores your data or where it sends and shares it. Personal confession: they used it after fights with a boyfriend or friend to write out what happened and ask who was right. That's very bad because ChatGPT keeps all that information somewhere.
7. Wrap-up: I've given you alternatives and serious reasons. If you keep using it, at least don't tell it too much, use it in a specific way, and always remember it may well be wrong.
8. Sign-off comment CTA: 'That's it for this video. Tell me in the comments how you like the Memo AI app and whether it saved you like it saved me.'

Remark 5 (overlay, 'and to finish'): the student got a 1 (fail) and asked if it could be kept spoiler-free for his parents. Joke: it's really not fair, at least wait for the parents' meeting. With e-diaries you used to be able to stay quiet until the meeting. Mum comes home: 'Do I have to blush every time at that parents' meeting?' At least you were alive until the meeting. Quick product aside (around 15 s, still in the same talking-head shot): if you want to learn in a fun way, go to the Memo AI page (memoai.eu). Back to the trick: turn your hands and count the folded fingers, 3 here and 2 here. Multiply them. These are small numbers, so it's easy: 6.
Reveal: the answer is 56, so 7 × 8 = 56.
